title: Add read-ahead and stale-reading re-check to the drain (A5)
summary: Build job A5 of the async drain (D145): while job N runs, the drain reads and plans hard jobs up to read_ahead items ahead, re-checking a reading for staleness when its job starts (design section 4). Follows job 20261029-142849-04d9, whose [drain.pipeline] config is kept as is. With max_in_flight = 1 the drain behaves as today. The audience is the maintainer who runs the drain and the verifier who checks it.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test, clippy -D warnings and fmt criteria.
Criteria run the drain through its entry point and observe read-ahead happening.
The check is read-ahead observed with max_in_flight above 1 and no change at 1.
Limited to the three named files.
Changelog and doc comments written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (entry points drain and drain_concurrent, Steps trait, Item, Limits) and docs/design/async-drain.md sections 4, 11 and 12 (read_ahead, job 5). No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are unaffected. The property is measured directly: tests drive drain/drain_concurrent with a fake Steps and count read and plan calls made before the prior job finishes.

Prior job 20261029-142849-04d9 (landed, verdict pass): its config.rs, CHANGELOG.md and design-doc work is kept and not edited here. Its findings are addressed as follows. The stale design-doc line 21 and the terse DrainPipeline error message are out of scope for this job. The MAX_CHECK_SLOTS_CEILING nit is not a defect and needs no fix. read_ahead is read from the existing Config.drain.pipeline, which needs no config change.
No new refusal rule is added, so no newly-refused-readings percentage applies.
Reading changes in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs are limited to what the stale-reading check needs, such as exposing the touched paths of a reading; if none is needed the file stays unchanged.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) do not change; athena.toml keeps max_in_flight = 1.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a new drain test with max_in_flight = 2 and read_ahead = 1, driven through drain_concurrent, shows the next item's read (and plan, if the job is hard) is requested while the current job is still running, and never more than read_ahead items ahead.

Run cargo test: a test shows that when the running job changes paths the read-ahead reading touches, that reading is marked stale and the touched paths are re-checked when the job starts; a reading whose paths are untouched is used as is.
Run cargo test: with max_in_flight = 1 no read-ahead happens, and the existing drain tests in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs pass unchanged (git diff shows no edits to existing test bodies).
Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test; all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing read-ahead and the stale-reading re-check, saying that max_in_flight = 1 is unchanged.
The change touches only crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (if needed) and CHANGELOG.md; git diff shows no edits to athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows.

out_of_scope: Editing athena.toml or raising max_in_flight to 3 (build job 10)
Changes to crates/athena-data/src/config.rs from job 20261029-142849-04d9 (kept as landed)
Fixing the stale line 21 in docs/design/async-drain.md and the DrainPipeline error wording from job 20261029-142849-04d9
Disk-guard, check-slot and conflict-return behavior (other build jobs)
departures: Hard concurrency change in a large drain.rs, so cost, time and pass chance are worse than the reference.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline: how the drain reads and plans jobs ahead, and when a reading is judged stale.
